instruction: Color Ramp Banding Driven by Object Info > Location.z `scene.blend` contains a vertical stack of 5 cubes `Cube_00`, `Cube_01`, `Cube_02`, `Cube_03`, `Cube_04` at world Z positions 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (spacing 1 BU). All 5 cubes share a single material `BandMat`, which is currently a plain grey Principled BSDF (no banding). A camera at (8, -8, 3) looks at the stack, and an area light illuminates the scene. The render engine is Cycles CPU (samples=32, seed=0, 256x256, denoiser on). modify `BandMat` so its shader graph uses a `ShaderNodeObjectInfo` node to read each object's Z location and drive a `ShaderNodeValToRGB` (Color Ramp). Each cube, sharing the SAME material datablock, should render in a distinct color determined by its own world Z position. Concretely: - Use `ShaderNodeObjectInfo` to read the per-object Location vector. - Use `ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ` (or any equivalent) to pull out the Z component. - Use Math nodes (e.g. SUBTRACT and/or DIVIDE) to remap Z in [0, 4] -> ramp input in [0, 1]. The simplest mapping is a single DIVIDE by 4. - Feed that remapped value into a `ShaderNodeValToRGB` (Color Ramp) with EXACTLY 5 stops at positions {0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0} (tolerance +/- 0.02) and colors: - position 0.00 -> RED (1, 0, 0) - position 0.25 -> ORANGE (1, 0.5, 0) - position 0.50 -> YELLOW (1, 1, 0) - position 0.75 -> GREEN (0, 1, 0) - position 1.00 -> BLUE (0, 0, 1) - Set the Color Ramp's interpolation mode to `CONSTANT` so each Z-band is a distinct flat color rather than a gradient. - Wire the ramp's Color output into the Principled BSDF's Base Color, and the BSDF into Material Output's Surface. Because all 5 cubes share the SAME material datablock, their individual colors come from Object Info's per-object Location output, not from distinct materials. Save the result to `answer.blend`. Requirements: 1. `answer.blend` opens as a valid Blender file. 2. 5 mesh objects named `Cube_00`... `Cube_04` exist, each at the expected world Z (0, 1, 2, 3, 4 respectively). 3. Material `BandMat` exists and uses nodes. 4. `BandMat`'s node tree contains both a `ShaderNodeObjectInfo` and a `ShaderNodeValToRGB`. 5. The Color Ramp has exactly 5 stops at positions {0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0} within tolerance 0.02. 6. The Color Ramp's interpolation mode is `CONSTANT`. 7. When rendered with a deterministic Cycles CPU configuration (seed=0, samples=32, 256x256, denoiser on), each cube projects to a pixel ROI in the image whose dominant color matches the expected band: - Cube at Z=0 -> RED (mean R > G, R > B, R > 0.5) - Cube at Z=1 -> ORANGE (R high, G medium, B low) - Cube at Z=2 -> YELLOW (R and G both high, B low) - Cube at Z=3 -> GREEN (G > R, G > B) - Cube at Z=4 -> BLUE (B > R, B > G)
